QUESTION: acme search-api results stopped being relevant right after this morning's index build in production. What is the documented recovery?
ASKED BY: Ananya Iyer (SRE on-call), tenant acme, environment production, at 2026-09-22T10:30:00Z

EVIDENCE:
[E1] RB-SRCH-004 · search-api: relevance drop after an index build — Recovery
Point the products alias back to the previous index build with the search-admin pipeline (search-admin alias products --to <previous-build>). The previous build id is in the index build record.

[E2] GX-RB-SRCH-001 · globex search-api: relevance drop after an index build — Recovery
globex keeps two live builds. Re-point the catalog alias to the standby build in the globex search console. No approval is needed during business hours.

[E3] RB-SRCH-004 · search-api: relevance drop after an index build — Approval
The search on-call approves the alias rollback. Keep the bad build for 48 hours for analysis.

[E4] INC-4630 · INC-4630 checkout-api p95 latency after 4.12.0 — Resolution
Latency recovered about 20 minutes after the restart. Follow-up found a missing index in 4.12.0; 4.12.1 fixed it. Action item: update RB-CHK-007 (done in v4).

[E5] INC-4733 · INC-4733 search-api relevance after products build — Summary
A synonyms change in the nightly build made shoe searches return socks. Search on-call approved an alias rollback to the previous build; relevance recovered immediately.

[E6] RN-CHK-4.17.0 · checkout-api 4.17.0 release notes — Changes
Cost efficiency release. Tuned the orders-db connection pool to cut idle connections. ORM upgrade. No schema migration.

[E7] INC-4512 · INC-4512 cart-api latency after 3.4.0 — Summary
cart-api p95 rose to 900 ms after 3.4.0 shrank the Redis pool. Rolled back to 3.3.9 through the pipeline with incident-commander approval; recovered in 6 minutes.

[E8] SEC-PM-2207 · Security postmortem: orders-db connection saturation on 30 August — Root cause
A leaked partner API token (partner P-1182, token prefix mrd_live_7731) drove a credential-stuffing burst against /v1/orders. Each request opened a database transaction, and the orders-db pool saturated.

QUESTION: acme order-history-api reads have been slow since the 08:30 deploy in production. What is the remediation?
ASKED BY: Ananya Iyer (SRE on-call), tenant acme, environment production, at 2026-09-22T10:30:00Z

EVIDENCE:
[E1] RB-OHA-001 · order-history-api: slow order reads — Remediation
Latency on GET /v1/orders after a deploy is almost always read amplification on the primary. Turn on read-replica routing with the feature flag oha.read_replica=on in the flag service. No approval is needed.

[E2] RB-CHK-007 · checkout-api: latency or errors after a deploy (automated rollback) — Remediation
From 1 October, release-bot rolls checkout-api back automatically when the deploy-correlation score is above 0.9. For SEV3 incidents no human approval is needed; incident-commander approval remains for SEV1 and SEV2.

[E3] RB-CHK-007 · checkout-api: latency or errors after a deploy — Remediation
Restart the checkout-api pods (kubectl rollout restart deployment/checkout-api) and scale to 10 replicas to drain the connection pool. If latency has not recovered within 15 minutes, roll the release back.

[E4] RB-CHK-007 · checkout-api: latency or errors after a deploy — Remediation
Roll the release back through the release pipeline (release-pipeline rollback checkout-api --to <previous-version>) to the last good version named in the deployment record. Do not restart pods or run kubectl rollout undo: a restart does not fix a regressed release, and the GitOps controller reverts direct changes.

[E5] RB-INV-004 · inventory-api: stale stock levels — Remediation
Trigger the warehouse resync job from the job runner (jobs run inv-resync --tenant acme). Stock converges within 10 minutes. No approval is needed.

[E6] RB-CHK-007 · checkout-api: latency or errors after a deploy — Diagnose
Open the deployment record of the release that preceded the alert and compare its config diff with the previous release: pool sizes, timeouts, ORM version. If the alert started within 60 minutes of the deploy and the diff touches the datasource, treat it as a release regression.

[E7] INC-4801 · INC-4801 order-history-api slow reads — Summary
GET /v1/orders p95 at 3 s after a page-size change. Turned on oha.read_replica; recovered in a minute.

[E8] SEC-PM-2207 · Security postmortem: orders-db connection saturation on 30 August — Remediation
Revoked the token, added per-partner rate limits, and moved partner tokens to the vault rotation schedule.

globex stock comes from the merchant's ERP feed. Run stock-reconcile from the globex scheduler (gx-sched run stock-reconcile); it replays the last ERP snapshot. No approval is needed.

[E6] RB-PRC-002 · pricing-api: stale promotions — Remediation
Run the promotion sync job (jobs run promo-sync --tenant acme). Do not edit prices in the database by hand.
